Jennifer Programming Language source snapshot (jennifer-HEAD)
SHA-256: 3b77bff1c9ed25c70428a3c4b2dacb01ccbb9d95c770c6f4027e02c18c8c61a8
Verdict: BENIGN
Marker / commit-body line:
Jennifer language: benign operator-list docs; parse arithmetic chains

Identification and behavior
---------------------------
This is the Go implementation of Jennifer, an interpreted language, with its
CLI, standard libraries, plain-text .j modules, examples, tests, documentation,
editor support, and distribution scripts. It is a source archive, not a built
interpreter. The archive does not pin a release number beyond its HEAD name.
README, go.mod, CLI banner, package namespaces, and file organization agree.

Execution traced: cmd/jennifer/main.go dispatches explicit commands. runFileHook
reads the supplied file/stdin, checks requirements, lexes and preprocesses it,
parses tokens, installs the builtin library registry, and invokes the interpreter.
Standard-library registration exposes functions; it does not automatically call
network or process operations. os.run/spawn take the Jennifer caller's argument
list and use exec.Command(argv[0], argv[1:]...). net.connect takes the caller's
host/port and uses Dial/DialTimeout; TLS configuration is likewise explicit.
The generated encoding init function registers character-codec lookup tables.
The encoding library exposes conversion functions to scripts; its tables and
Base64 routines are not a hidden stage. Build scripts generate version metadata
and compile Go/TinyGo binaries. No concealed payload, unsolicited collection,
autorun change, or independent command/control path was established in this review.
The ordinary language capabilities and packaging tip the verdict; no machine
installation history, invocation, or user-supplied .j program was provided.

Decisive version comparison
---------------------------
Retrieved ORIGINAL GitHub source tarballs with forager (not reconstructed):
https://github.com/jennifer-language/jennifer/archive/refs/tags/0.14.0.tar.gz
https://github.com/jennifer-language/jennifer/archive/refs/tags/0.24.0.tar.gz
An initial attempt at the release-checklist example 0.14.1 returned HTTP 404;
remote tags confirmed 0.14.0 exists. Downloads and .forage.json provenance remain
in scratch/version-drift/prior and scratch/version-drift/earlier.

Release 0.14.0 has zero hostile/suspicious findings under the original rules.
Its rejected.md is Markdown; the current member is heuristically treated as
Python (with a recorded parse-abandonment diagnostic). BOTH contain the same
operator list: + - * / // % & | ^ ~ << >>. It occurs in the rejection of range
literal syntax, explaining that other operators work in multiple contexts.
It is backtick-delimited prose enumerating tokens, with no operands or runtime
effects. The text matcher mistook glyph order for arithmetic and concealment.
The later 0.24.0 release also fires under the original rules: this is not a new
hostile operation unique to the supplied HEAD snapshot. Its operator paragraph
is unchanged. Current document additions discuss mutable/reference closures
and edit wording/links. go.mod is identical between 0.24.0 and this snapshot.
Reviewed execution-path changes include process-stream redirection, stable child
handles, bounded waits, explicit source-file shebang support, and network timeout
and API changes. They remain script-invoked interpreter/library functionality.
Saved document, main, process, and network diffs are in scratch/version-drift.

Rule correction and coverage audit
----------------------------------
Removed the arithmetic-expression-chains rule from
objectives/anti-static/obfuscation/eval/scripting/reflection/advanced-python.yaml.
Its regex requires neither obfuscation, evaluation, nor reflection, so this
placement, suspicious criticality, and inherited T1027/E1014 claims were unsupported.
Replaced it with micro-behaviors/data/arithmetic::python-multiply-floor-or-shift-chain,
a notable parsed-expression observation. The expression must contain the same
ordered multiplication, floor division, OR, and shift sequence; quoted/commented
expressions are excluded. No filename or product-identity allowlist was added.
This detects mechanics without treating ordinary calculations as concealment.

Exact-ID consumer audit found only a negative symbol-table fixture, updated to
the new ID. Three ancestor-directory consumers select anti-static/obfuscation:
concealed-credential-exfiltration-channel, long-tail-build-config-payload, and
suspicious-hidden-listener. All are file-scoped JavaScript/TypeScript composites;
the removed atom was Python-only and cannot supply their same-file evidence.
There are no directory consumers of the new arithmetic home or its ancestors.
No caller was broadened to substitute arithmetic for required concealment.

Inspected existing fixture/source corpus and named sample files, including
bounded decompression and 669 Python members of ZIP-compatible artifacts.
The only raw legacy-pattern match found was the supplied document; no existing
positive attack fixture for the removed rule was found. Real parsed chains and
parenthesized chains remain detectable in focused controls. Operator tables,
quoted text inside concatenation, comments, and the original prose excerpt are
negative controls; a true chain alongside an operator table remains positive.
The existing hostile compressed-source-evaluation.py fixture retains its exact
trait set (including compressed-code execution/concealment) before and after.
No material supported attack detection was lost in these checks.

  After:  hostile 0; suspicious 0; classifier BENIGN, probability 0.39660186.
  rejected.md static risk: 38 -> 8. Outer aggregate risk: 147 -> 117.
Only removal: the unsupported arithmetic obfuscation trait in rejected.md and
its root aggregate. Every other member trait is retained; no new finding on the
sample. No remaining rule/classifier disagreement with the BENIGN judgement.
The queue's score 40 differs from the reproduced member risk 38 on this engine.
Classifier version v18.18; engine 2.13.0 warns that its feature specification is
older than v21. These probabilities are classifier outputs, not verdict evidence.

An initial default-follow scan also analyzed linked remote resources. It was
repeated with --follow=none so the recorded comparison measures the supplied
archive and its own members, without conflating separately fetched artifacts.
